method: Each listed PNG was opened with view_image and visually inspected. No image edits or denoising were applied to these unfiltered progressive renders.
findings: Historic frontage, entrance arches, broad stair and two authored bronze lions remain identifiable in day and night.
Modern Wing night refinement reveals the projecting white roof and glazed pavilions; illumination follows primary nighttime reference cues.
The t240 gallery has neutral lighting, legible original geometric artwork, plain plaster soffits and readable wall/frame details.
The t225 Griffin Court route is open, with visible columns, glazed roof and an unobstructed east gallery portal.
Nichols Bridgeway follows its mapped rising alignment toward the Modern Wing terrace; rail and deck geometry are present.
limitations: Fine Monte Carlo grain remains in these unfiltered 128-sample stills; this report does not certify motion noise performance.
Interior rooms and artwork are authored interpretations, not a recreation of the current exhibition layout.
Bronze lions use authored anatomical primitives, not photogrammetry.
Later campus wings and the immediate open grounds are simplified relative to the featured museum fronts.
Fixture powers and positions are visual approximations rather than a photometric survey.
